index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates an auto-regressive video generation framework divided into two main stages: 'First Frame Initialization' and 'Auto-Regressive Generation', each enclosed in a dashed rectangular boundary. In the left section, 'First Frame Initialization', a green box labeled y⁰ represents the initial anchor frame. This frame is generated by combining inputs from three sources: a light blue box labeled 'User', another light blue box labeled 'T2I' (Text-to-Image), and a medium blue box labeled 'ART•V'. All three inputs feed into y⁰ via solid black arrows, indicating their contribution to initializing the first frame. From y⁰, a solid arrow extends rightward toward the next stage, while a curved arrow loops back to the right edge of the initialization box, suggesting continuation or feedback into the subsequent process.

The right section, 'Auto-Regressive Generation', shows a sequence of five horizontally aligned boxes representing consecutive frames: y^{i−2}, y^{i−1}, y^i, y^{i+1}, and y^{i+2}. These boxes are color-coded: y^{i−2} and y^{i−1} are red, y^i is orange, and y^{i+1} and y^{i+2} are gray, visually distinguishing past, current, and future frames. Below this sequence, a medium blue box labeled 'ART•V' receives two inputs: a 'Reference' signal from the past frames y^{i−2} and y^{i−1} (via a curved bracket and arrow), and an 'Anchor' signal from the green y⁰ box located below it. Additionally, a 'Text' input enters ART•V from the right side. The output of ART•V is directed upward to the current frame y^i, indicating that the model generates the next frame based on the reference, anchor, and text. Dotted lines extend from both sides of the Auto-Regressive Generation box, implying that this process continues iteratively for further frames. The overall layout emphasizes a sequential, step-by-step generation pipeline where the initial frame y⁰ serves as a persistent anchor throughout the entire auto-regressive process.
